\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سائرن} (sāiran)}{سائرن (sāiran)}]{\ur{سائرن} (sāiran) — a siren}

\label{lesson:UR-C289-sairan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for brightness, then the Urdu for scorching heat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سائرن}}
\textbf{\ur{سائرن}} — \emph{sāiran} — \textquotedblleft{}a siren\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سائرن} \ur{سن} \ur{کر} \ur{سب} \ur{باہر} \ur{آئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāiran sun kar sab bāhar āe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Hearing the siren, everyone came outside.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سائرن}} (\emph{sāiran}) is borrowed from English \emph{siren}. Fire engines, ambulances and the police all have one.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāiran}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāiran}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāiran sun kar sab bāhar āe.} — Hearing the siren, everyone came outside.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for brightness, then the Urdu for scorching heat, then say \emph{sāiran} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سائرن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A siren\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عملہ} (amlā)}{عملہ (amlā)}]{\ur{عملہ} (amlā) — the staff; a crew}

\label{lesson:UR-C289-amla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for scorching heat, then the Urdu for a siren.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عملہ}}
\textbf{\ur{عملہ}} — \emph{amlā} — \textquotedblleft{}the staff; a crew\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{عملے} \ur{نے} \ur{آگ} \ur{بجھائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{amle ne āg bujhāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The crew put the fire out.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عملہ}} (\emph{amlā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿamala}, \textquotedblleft{}workers\textquotedblright{}: the people who do the work of an office, a hospital or a fire station.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amlā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amlā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amle ne āg bujhāī.} — The crew put the fire out.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for scorching heat, then the Urdu for a siren, then say \emph{amlā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بجھنا} (bujhnā)}{بجھنا (bujhnā)}]{\ur{بجھنا} (bujhnā) — to go out (of a fire); to go dark}

\label{lesson:UR-C289-bujhna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a siren, then the Urdu for a crew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بجھنا}}
\textbf{\ur{بجھنا}} — \emph{bujhnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to go out (of a fire); to go dark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{صبح} \ur{تک} \ur{آگ} \ur{بجھ} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{subah tak āg bujh gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
By morning the fire had gone out.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{چراغ} \ur{بجھ} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh chirāgh bujh gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bujhnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be extinguished\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*vijjhāyati}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 11703). It is the partner of \textbf{\ur{بجھانا}}: you \textbf{\ur{بجھانا}} a fire, and it \textbf{\ur{بجھنا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bujhnā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a siren, then the Urdu for a crew, then say \emph{bujhnā} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پگھلنا} (pighalnā)}{پگھلنا (pighalnā)}]{\ur{پگھلنا} (pighalnā) — to melt}

\label{lesson:UR-C289-pighalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a crew, then the Urdu for to go out (of a fire).

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پگھلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پگھلنا}} — \emph{pighalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to melt\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{برف} \ur{پگھلی}, \emph{voh barf pighlī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پگھلنا}} (\emph{pighalnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pighalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be melted\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 8486).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہڑبڑانا} (haṛbaṛānā)}{ہڑبڑانا (haṛbaṛānā)}]{\ur{ہڑبڑانا} (haṛbaṛānā) — to rush in a panic; to fumble}

\label{lesson:UR-C289-harbarana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to go out (of a fire), then the Urdu for to melt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہڑبڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ہڑبڑانا}} — \emph{haṛbaṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rush in a panic; to fumble\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سائرن} \ur{سن} \ur{کر} \ur{سب} \ur{ہڑبڑا} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sāiran sun kar sab haṛbaṛā gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When they heard the siren, everyone rushed about in a panic.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{ہڑبڑا} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh haṛbaṛā gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہڑبڑانا}} (\emph{haṛbaṛānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{haṛbaṛānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to hurry\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{haṛbaṛī}, \textquotedblleft{}confusion\textquotedblright{}, under a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 13949). The doubled sound is the scramble itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{haṛbaṛānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāiran sun kar sab haṛbaṛā gae.} — When they heard the siren, everyone rushed about in a panic.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to go out (of a fire), then the Urdu for to melt, then say \emph{haṛbaṛānā} again
\end{itemize}
